I wrote `src/mode-limits.ts`. `useModeLimits` assigns the mode's `GeospatialLimits` object to `camera.limits` without modifying it, then re-writes the current `radius` and `yaw` so the existing pose is clamped to the new mode's ranges right away. I could not compile or run it, since the library isn't on this machine, so the behaviour rests on your notes (items 18, 21 and 22), not on the library source.

I'm not sure of three things:
- The re-write relies on the setters clamping even when the value doesn't change. If the setter skips equal values, the current pose won't be clamped on a mode switch until the next write.
- Note 21 says yaw and pitch are clamped to `camera.limits`, but I'm not certain the radius setter uses the same range logic as `clampZoomDistance`, which takes a zoom distance.
- The library's own writes (flights, `attachGeospatialControls`) may not all go through these setters. I only covered writes the app makes.
